author: Edge
text:
Kohai wrote: So, as Staurum suggested, I re-read the FTR article and found many new information which I did not see previously.

For example, an FTR is made after a break of these barriers:

1. An SR line which are two or more highs/lows lined, in this case, the higher the number of highs/lows, the stronger the FTR that is generated when the level breaks 2. Another FTR in the opposite direction 3. A PAZ limit

OK, let's find some FTRs of the first type. (As always, correct me if I'm wrong)

It can also be a single high or low. Obviously the ones that have more that line up, have more stops beyond them. As you go through the material, over time some others may pop out like breaks of cp, ls but don't worry about those yet. What you have outlined is spot on IMO.

The logic consequence is that breaking this level requires a lot of orders and when the levels breaks, the stop losses of the retailers and small funds are taken. The fact is that the SL is an order that pushes price in the direction of the break, so many pending orders remains at the FTR.
